Link order and locks

0 / 6

Numbers set the link order; the last connects to the first. P1–P12 label candidate positions here. Use the placed count: in-game 7/8 means 7 placed, 8 activated; newly activated Starshards join after a reset.

Constellation bonus · Client rules

Reset costs and budget

Uses a fixed lock count and base fees from 1.5.002. Recalculate when the lock count changes.

Bonus reference

By default, enter the integer area shown in-game. Verified client rounding converts it into bonuses (e.g. 57% area at a 20% multiplier = 11.39%). Uncheck to estimate enclosed geometric area, round it down, then apply the same client conversion. The same-version 68.8996% → 68% sample supports this estimate; server precision and degenerate boundaries remain incompletely verified. Editing positions does not change the entered in-game area; update it yourself.

This browser saves configurations and progress for all 10 constellations.

Constellation overview

Bonus plans

The official guide confirms earlier constellation bonuses remain active together. Checked plans are totaled here. In-game areas use client rules; geometric estimates round area down first. Plans without an area are excluded from the numeric total.

Starshard unlock requirements

Original requirements table ↗

Activate every Starshard in a constellation to unlock the next. The official first-constellation guide refers to Cookie slots; the configuration records stage thresholds. Check actual automatic activation in-game.

Reset fee table and rules

Official placement probabilities

Complete configurations of positions and link order have equal probability; different areas need not. Area and bonuses derive from the configuration, without a separate roll. The table gives the probability of one specific complete configuration with no locks.

Locked Starshards keep their order and positions; all remaining legal configurations are equally likely. For N Starshards and L locks, this implies P(12−L, N−L) remaining configurations. This is a combinatorial derivation; no separate official locked-Starshard table is published.
